name: Persistent Müllerian Duct Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Persistent Müllerian Duct Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of uterus and fallopian tubes in a genetically and phenotypically male individual
Identification of mutations in AMH or AMHR2 genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of Müllerian duct derivatives in a 46,XY individual with supporting genetic testing confirming AMH or AMHR2 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by imaging and genetic testing; surgical exploration may be necessary.

laboratory: Normal male hormone profile (testosterone, LH, FSH)
Elevated or absent Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) levels depending on mutation
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing presence of uterus and fallopian tubes in male pelvis
Inguinal hernia containing Müllerian structures on imaging

distinguishingFeatures: Absent Müllerian structures due to normal AMH function
Elevated testosterone with androgen receptor defects

redFlags: Presence of Müllerian structures in phenotypic male
Risk of malignant transformation in retained Müllerian remnants
references: Orphanet: Persistent Müllerian Duct Syndrome - ORPHA2856
